justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 through R-03 directly: Real-Time Scoring Service evaluates authorizations, Case Management Backend handles flagged reviews via Case Workflow Engine, and AWS CodeDeploy alongside dynamic S3 rules loading enables zero-downtime scoring and model updates.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 req/s is supported by Go on ECS Fargate, In-Process Go Cache, DynamoDB Feature Cache via VPC endpoints, and asynchronous auditing via Messaging & Event Bus. However, routing ingress through Amazon API Gateway and Lambda introduces latency overhead.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture supports Payment Gateway integration via gRPC and HTTPS/mTLS. While Card Networks / Tokenization Vault is identified in the System Context diagram, container and component diagrams omit direct interactions between the scoring pipeline and the external token vault.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers access the system via HTTPS and ZTNA/SSO. However, only Case Management Backend is modeled without any dedicated UI, frontend client, or portal container to support analyst case review workflows.
justifications.reliability: High availability is addressed through Circuit Breaker & Fallback Engine in API Gateway, Fallback Circuit Breaker Component in Go, and CloudWatch Synthetics Canary, ensuring payment processing is not blocked for over one minute during scoring outages.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS compliance is strictly observed: PAN avoidance via Card Networks / Tokenization Vault, payload sanitization in Audit & Evidence Assembler, KMS encryption, AWS WAF, and tamper-evident 7-year storage via Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode.
justifications.maintainability: Responsibilities are cleanly partitioned between Real-Time Scoring Service and Case Management Backend. Leveraging managed services (Fargate, DynamoDB, SQS, Firehose) aligns well with the 3-engineer operational constraint, though tight coupling to proprietary AWS primitives limits modular component replacement.
justifications.portability: The system is tailored for AWS eu-west-1 using ECS Fargate, DynamoDB, SQS/SNS, Kinesis Firehose, and S3 Object Lock. While well-adapted to the target cloud, deep proprietary AWS lock-in significantly restricts portability to on-premises or alternate cloud providers.

PERF-01.justification: Routing all authorization traffic through API Gateway and a Lambda circuit breaker before reaching Fargate introduces invocation and serialization overheads that jeopardize the 50 ms P99 latency budget under 3,000 RPS.
sensitivity_points: Lambda execution overhead in the synchronous request path
DynamoDB VPC endpoint read latency under 3,000 RPS
tradeoffs: Serverless ingress components reduce operational burden but introduce latency jitter

PERF-02.justification: The Case Management Backend runs in a dedicated Fargate container querying Aurora PostgreSQL, completely isolated from the Go scoring service and DynamoDB feature cache used for authorization decisions.
sensitivity_points: Physical isolation between scoring infrastructure and analyst review queries
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual data stores increases consistency management complexity for operational data

AVAIL-01.justification: The ingress layer incorporates an AWS Lambda circuit breaker and fallback engine that executes default decisions if the scoring service fails, while emitting audit events to prevent payment blocking.
sensitivity_points: Circuit breaker failure detection thresholds and execution timeout settings
Reliability of fallback audit emission without real-time scoring containers
tradeoffs: Failing open or closed maintains payment flow but risks fraud exposure or false declines

AVAIL-02.justification: The scoring service publishes audit events asynchronously using SNS and buffered SQS FIFO queues with DLQs, completely decoupling scoring latency and continuity from downstream audit persistence issues.
sensitivity_points: SQS queue retention limits and dead-letter queue buffering capacity
Asynchronous SDK non-blocking publish call durations
tradeoffs: Asynchronous buffering guarantees sub-50ms latency but introduces eventual audit persistence

MOD-01.justification: AWS CodeDeploy provides automated canary deployments, while the scoring engine dynamically loads signed model binaries from S3 and tags every scored decision with the active model version.
sensitivity_points: CodeDeploy canary health-check duration and rollback automation triggers
In-process model binary verification and hot-reloading stability
tradeoffs: Canary deployments lengthen deployment cycles slightly to ensure zero-downtime safety

MOD-02.justification: Dynamic loading of rules from S3 and cache invalidation via SNS/SQS enable rules to activate within one hour without service downtime, while decision explanations are captured by the scoring engine.
sensitivity_points: Eventual consistency delay of cache invalidation across distributed Go scoring containers
Rule syntax validation prior to dynamic runtime loading
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule reloading without container restarts increases runtime engine parsing complexity

SEC-01.justification: PANs are never stored, tokenization is enforced externally, and the Audit & Evidence Assembler sanitizes payloads before presentation. However, specific UEBA detection mechanisms for 15-minute anomaly alerting are only generic.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of field-level masking in the Audit & Evidence Assembler
Alerting threshold latency within CloudWatch and X-Ray telemetry
tradeoffs: Restricting analyst access to tokens simplifies compliance but impedes manual investigation

SEC-02.justification: Audit payloads with inputs, model versions, and explanations are stored via Kinesis Firehose into S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode and transitioned to Glacier, enabling retrieval within hours.
sensitivity_points: WORM compliance retention configuration preventing premature object deletion
Glacier Flexible Retrieval job initiation and restore turnaround times
tradeoffs: Glacier tiering drastically reduces 7-year storage costs but requires hours to restore data

elements: Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers
